visuals.title: Where it happens
visuals.text: The pharynx collapses during sleep; the brain wakes briefly to reopen it.

visuals.title: Complications
visuals.text: Hypertension, heart failure and stroke; polycythaemia; sleepiness causing accidents and driving risk.

events.x: Weight loss, less alcohol, sleep hygiene

glossary.Upper airway: The nose, mouth, pharynx and larynx, above the trachea.
glossary.Intermittent hypoxia: Repeated short drops in blood oxygen, as happens with each apnoea.
glossary.Fragmented sleep: Sleep broken up by many brief awakenings, so it is not restful.
glossary.BMI: Body mass index: weight in kg divided by height in metres squared; 30 or more is obese.
glossary.Obesity: Excess body fat, defined as a BMI of 30 or more.
glossary.Anatomical obstruction: A structural cause of a narrow airway, such as large tonsils or a small jaw.
glossary.Sedatives: Drugs that cause drowsiness, such as benzodiazepines and opioids, which relax airway muscles.
glossary.Snoring: Noise from vibrating soft tissues in a partly narrowed upper airway during sleep.
glossary.Heart failure: When the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Stroke: Brain damage from a blocked or burst blood vessel in the brain.
glossary.Ventilatory drive: The brain's signal to breathe, set mainly by carbon dioxide levels.
glossary.Respiratory rate: The number of breaths per minute.
glossary.Sleep study: An overnight test recording breathing, oxygen levels and sleep.
glossary.Screening questionnaire: A short set of questions used to pick out people likely to have a condition before testing.
glossary.Weight loss: The most important lifestyle measure in OSA, reducing fat around the pharynx.
glossary.Overnight ventilation: Breathing support given while asleep, here by CPAP keeping the airway open.
glossary.Pharyngeal: Relating to the pharynx, the throat behind the nose and mouth.
glossary.Muscle tone: The background tension in a muscle, which falls during sleep.
glossary.Sympathetic activation: Switching on the fight-or-flight nervous system, raising heart rate and blood pressure.
glossary.Systemic hypertension: High blood pressure in the body's main circulation, as opposed to the lungs.
glossary.Positive airway pressure: Air pressure kept above atmospheric pressure inside the airway.
glossary.Respiratory cycle: One full breath in and out.
glossary.Splinting: Holding a structure open or still; CPAP air pressure holds the pharynx open.
